column3: The Greek begins with collective “all that,” rendered as personal “everyone.”
“Can” is supplied in the question; the Greek explicitly says “now.”
“Only” makes the exclusiveness explicit rather than translating a separate word in the final clause.
The Greek has “and” rather than concessive “yet.”
BSB places “for the life of the world” with giving; the Greek places it after identifying the bread as His flesh.
“Began” is supplied; “this man” makes the Greek demonstrative explicit.
BSB’s “your fathers” and “the manna” match the Textus Receptus (μάννα); the critical text lacks them.
The Greek calls this a hard “word” and asks who can “hear” it; BSB uses “teaching” and “accept.”
